docs.title: wheels_builder
docs.text: Scripts to automate building and managing Python wheels for the Digital Research Alliance of Canada (DRAC) wheelhouse.

docs.title: Workflow Overview
docs.text:
Building and publishing wheels to the centralized wheelhouse typically follows a three-step workflow:

  1. Build or Adapt: Compile wheels from source with build_wheel.sh (or batch build with parbuild_wheel.sh).
  2. Inspect Compatibility: Use wheel_architecture.sh to verify library linkage, glibc compatibility, and detect target microarchitecture.
  3. Deploy: Copy wheels into the appropriate wheelhouse directory and adjust permissions with cp_wheels.sh.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• build_wheel.sh Build wheel(s) for a Python package from source across standard Python versions.
  • wheel_architecture.sh Analyzes wheel contents, checks glibc and library dependencies, and predicts the destination wheelhouse directory.
  • cp_wheels.sh Copies built wheels to their target location in the CVMFS wheelhouse with proper permissions.
  • parbuild_wheel.sh Builds multiple packages or versions in parallel across available CPU cores.
  • unmanylinuxize.sh Downloads pre-built manylinux wheels and patches RPATHs and metadata for the DRAC stack.
  • config/<package>.sh Configuration recipes providing custom hooks and build variables for specific packages.
  • manipulate_wheels.py Inspects and modifies wheel metadata, requirements, and local tags without rebuilding.

docs.title: Build a wheel for a specific version
docs.text: $ bash build_wheel.sh --package <name> --version <version> --verbose 3

docs.title: Inspect wheel placement
docs.text: $ bash wheel_architecture.sh <wheel_file>.whl

docs.title: Deploy to wheelhouse
docs.text: $ bash cp_wheels.sh --remove --wheel <wheel_file>.whl

docs.title: build_wheel.sh
docs.text:
Build wheel(s) for a Python package.

This script will:

  • Create a build-virtualenv based on the Python version and install any dependencies.
  • Download the package from PyPI (by default), either the version specified or else the latest.
  • Build the wheel.
  • Add the +computecanada local version tag to the wheel name.
  • Automatically inspect and adjust NumPy and PyTorch requirements if shared libraries link against them.
  • Install the wheel into the build-virtualenv and try to import it.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Usage: build_wheel.sh --package <python package name>
         [--version <specific version>]
         [--python <comma separated list of python versions>]
         [--recursive=<1|0>]
         [--keep-build-dir]
         [--autocopy]
         [--no-verify]
         [--verbose=<1,2,3>]
         [--job]
         [--dependency=<dependency>]
         [--cpus|--job-cores=<number of cpus>]
         [--mem-cpu=<memory per cpu>[mM|gG]]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description Default --package <name> Python package name to build (required). --version <version> Specific version to build. If omitted, downloads latest from PyPI. Latest --python <versions> Comma-separated list of Python versions to build for (e.g. 3.11,3.12). Available versions in current StdEnv --recursive <1\|0> Whether to recursively build downloaded dependencies. 1 (enabled) --keep-build-dir Retain the temporary build directory (/tmp/build_wheels_tmp.$$) instead of deleting it. 0 (disabled) --autocopy Automatically call cp_wheels.sh --remove upon successful build. 0 (disabled) --no-verify Skip checking source files for -march=native or -xHost flags. 0 (verification active) --verbose <1,2,3> Verbosity level for commands and logs (1: commands, 2: commands + output on failure, 3: full stream). 0 --job Submit the build command as a Slurm batch job using sbatch. 0 (runs locally) --dependency <dep> Slurm job dependency specification passed to sbatch (e.g. afterok:<jobid>). None --cpus / --job-cores <N> Number of CPU cores requested for the Slurm job. 1 --mem-cpu <size> Memory per CPU requested for the Slurm job (e.g. 3G, 8000M). 3G

docs.title: Standard Environment & Architecture
docs.text:
By default, build_wheel.sh adapts its compiler and module environment to the currently loaded Standard Environment (EBVERSIONGENTOO):

  • StdEnv 2026 (2026): Uses GCC 15.3, Cython 3.3.0, NumPy 2.5.3, Rust, and builds for Python 3.14+ (excludes $\le$ 3.13).
  • StdEnv 2023 (2023): Uses GCC 12.3, Cython 3.2.4, NumPy 2.4.2, Rust, and builds for Python 3.11 to 3.14 (excludes $\le$ 3.10).

To build architecture-optimized wheels: - In StdEnv 2023 and 2026: load module load arch/avx2 (maps to x86-64-v3) or module load arch/avx512 (maps to x86-64-v4).

When -march=native is encountered in package sources, build_wheel.sh automatically rewrites it to target the active architecture (x86-64-v3 / x86-64-v4 in 2023+ or core-avx2 / skylake-avx512 in 2020), unless --no-verify is given.

docs.title: Automatic Requirement Adjustment & Tagging
docs.text:
1. NumPy: If compiled extensions contain references to NumPy C API, build_wheel.sh inspects the build version:
  2. For NumPy 1.x builds, it pins the minimum required NumPy version and adds <2.0.
  3. For NumPy 2.x builds, minimum version pinning is skipped.
  4. PyTorch: If compiled extensions link against libtorch.so (or if TORCH_VERSION is specified in configuration), build_wheel.sh:
  5. Pins a compatible PyTorch version (torch (~=X.Y.0)).
  6. If a wheel with the same version already exists in the central wheelhouse, it tags the new wheel with +torchXY.computecanada to avoid collisions.
  7. Pure Python & ABI3 wheels:
  8. If the built wheel is pure Python (py3-none-any, py2.py3-none-any) or ABI3 compatible (cp*-abi3), build_wheel.sh finishes after the first Python version since the artifact is compatible with all versions.

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
build_wheel.sh assumes standard package and module naming, but packages needing customization can define a configuration file in config/: 1. config/${PACKAGE}-${VERSION}.sh 2. config/${PACKAGE}.sh

See the Configuration Guide for available variables and hooks.

docs.title: Build latest version
docs.text:
Builds the latest version from PyPI for all default Python versions in the current environment: 

$ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython

docs.title: Build specific package version
docs.text: $ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython --version 1.84 --verbose 3

docs.title: Build specific Python version
docs.text: $ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython --python 3.14 --verbose 3

docs.title: Disable recursive dependency builds
docs.text: $ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython --recursive 0

docs.title: Keep build directory for debugging
docs.text:
Preserves the temporary build directory under /tmp to inspect build logs or patched source files: 

$ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython --version 1.84 --keep-build-dir

docs.title: Automatically copy upon success
docs.text: $ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython --autocopy

docs.title: Submit a build job with Slurm
docs.text:
$ bash build_wheel.sh --package biopython --version 1.84 --verbose 3 --job --cpus 4 --mem-cpu 8G
Submitted batch job 4680
This creates a batch job output log (biopython-1.84-<jobid>.log) in the current directory.

docs.title: Submit a chained dependent job
docs.text:
Submit a build job that starts only after another job finishes successfully: 

$ bash build_wheel.sh --package scipy --job --dependency afterok:4680

docs.title: Configuration Recipes
docs.text:
Configuration files provide package-specific customization or steps required to build or patch a Python wheel. One can create version-specific configuration files using ${PACKAGE}-${VERSION}.sh or general ones using ${PACKAGE}.sh.

build_wheel.sh and unmanylinuxize.sh search the config/ directory and source configuration files in the following order: 1. ${PACKAGE}-${VERSION}.sh 2. ${PACKAGE}.sh

To inspect practical recipes, browse the config/*.sh files in the repository.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
The following diagram illustrates the execution flow in build_wheel.sh and where each configuration hook executes:

flowchart TD
    A[Start build_wheel.sh] --> B[Source config/package.sh]
    B --> C["PRE_SETUP_COMMANDS"]
    C --> D[Create build virtualenv & install PYTHON_DEPS]
    D --> E["PRE_DOWNLOAD_COMMANDS"]
    E --> F[Download source archive / repository]
    F --> G["POST_DOWNLOAD_COMMANDS"]
    G --> H[Extract archive]
    H --> I["Apply PATCHES (from patches/)"]
    I --> J["PRE_BUILD_COMMANDS & Arch Checks"]
    J --> K[Build wheel with pip or setup.py]
    K --> L["POST_BUILD_COMMANDS"]
    L --> M[Inspect & Adjust Requirements: NumPy / PyTorch]
    M --> N["PRE_TEST_COMMANDS"]
    N --> O[Install wheel in test virtualenv & test imports]
    O --> P[Done / Optional autocopy]

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Description PACKAGE Name of the package. Defaults to --package. VERSION Version of the package. Defaults to --version or latest from PyPI. PYTHON_VERSIONS List of Python versions to build for. Defaults to active versions in the current StdEnv (e.g. 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 in 2023; 3.14+ in 2026). BDIST_WHEEL_ARGS Extra arguments passed to python setup.py bdist_wheel $BDIST_WHEEL_ARGS. PIP_WHEEL_ARGS Extra arguments passed to pip wheel $PIP_WHEEL_ARGS. MODULE_BUILD_DEPS EasyBuild/Lmod modules loaded specifically for building the wheel. MODULE_BUILD_DEPS_DEFAULT Default modules loaded for building: dynamically includes $NUMPY_MODULE, python-build-bundle, pytest, cython/$CYTHON_VERSION, and rust. MODULE_RUNTIME_DEPS Modules loaded during both building and testing of the wheel. PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_CMD Custom download command (defaults to pip download -v --no-cache --no-binary :all: --no-use-pep517 --no-build-isolation --no-deps $PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_ARGUMENT). PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_ARGUMENT Argument passed to download command (default: $PACKAGE==$VERSION or $PACKAGE). PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_NAME Archive name if different from $PACKAGE (default: $PACKAGE). PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_METHOD Set to "Git" when checking out source code from a git repository. PACKAGE_FOLDER_NAME Directory name of the extracted archive if different from $PACKAGE. PACKAGE_SUFFIX Suffix to append to the package name in setup.py (e.g. -cpu or -gpu). PATCHES Space-separated list of patch files in the patches/ directory to apply with patch -p1. PATCH_WHEEL_COMMANDS Shell commands to patch an already-built wheel (used when downloaded as .whl or under unmanylinuxize.sh). PRE_SETUP_COMMANDS Shell commands executed before creating the build virtualenv. PRE_DOWNLOAD_COMMANDS Shell commands executed before downloading the package source. POST_DOWNLOAD_COMMANDS Shell commands executed immediately after downloading the package. PRE_BUILD_COMMANDS Shell commands executed immediately before compiling the wheel. POST_BUILD_COMMANDS Shell commands executed after the wheel is built. PRE_TEST_COMMANDS Shell commands executed inside the test environment before verifying module imports. PYTHON_DEPS Additional Python dependencies installed into the build virtualenv via pip install. PYTHON_DEPS_DEFAULT Default build Python packages: setuptools>70 pip>=25.0. PYTHON_IMPORT_NAME Module name to import if different from package name (e.g. PACKAGE=pyzmq vs import zmq). PYTHON_TESTS Python code executed via python -c "import $NAME; $TESTS" to verify wheel functionality. TEST_COMMAND Custom shell command to run for testing instead of standard import testing. RPATH_TO_ADD Colon-separated paths to append to binary RPATHs via setrpaths.sh --add_path $RPATH_TO_ADD. RPATH_ADD_ORIGIN If set, runs setrpaths.sh --add_origin. UPDATE_REQUIREMENTS Requirements to modify using manipulate_wheels.py after building.

docs.title: cp_wheels.sh
docs.text: Copies all wheels in the current directory to the predicted location in the wheelhouse after adjusting file permissions (chmod ug+rw,o+r).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Usage: cp_wheels.sh [--wheel <wheel file>] [--arch generic|<rsnt_arch>]
                    [--remove] [--dry-run] [--force]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --wheel <wheel file> Process only this specific wheel file (otherwise processes all *computecanada*.whl files in the current working directory). --arch generic\|<rsnt_arch> Copy to a generic or architecture-specific directory. --remove Delete the local wheel file after successful copy. --dry-run Print copy and removal commands without executing them. --force Overwrite existing wheels in the wheelhouse (uses cp -v). By default, cp_wheels.sh prevents overwriting existing wheels with cp -vn (no-clobber).

docs.title: Architecture & Compatibility Rules
docs.text: If cp_wheels.sh detects an architecture-specific wheel, it refuses to copy it as generic unless the --arch flag is provided. The script considers a wheel to be architecture-specific if: 1. It links external libraries outside the standard compatibility layer, or 2. Existing wheels for the same package are already located in arch-specific directories in the wheelhouse.

docs.title: Valid Architectures by Standard Environment
docs.text:
• StdEnv 2023 and 2026 (EBVERSIONGENTOO >= 2023):
  • generic
  • x86-64-v3
  • x86-64-v4 Generic wheels built under StdEnv 2026 are routed to gentoo2026, and wheels built under StdEnv 2023 are routed to gentoo2023.
  • StdEnv 2020 (EBVERSIONGENTOO == 2020):
  • generic
  • sse3
  • avx
  • avx2
  • avx512

If an unknown compatibility layer is detected, run bash wheel_architecture.sh <wheel> to inspect the linkage and compatibility issues.

docs.title: Copy all wheels and remove local copies
docs.text:
Processes all *computecanada*.whl files in the current directory: 

$ bash cp_wheels.sh --remove

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text:
Inspect the predicted destination and actions without copying or deleting files: 

$ bash cp_wheels.sh --dry-run

docs.title: Copy specific wheel
docs.text: $ bash cp_wheels.sh --remove --wheel fastrlock-0.8.3+computecanada-cp313-cp313-linux_x86_64.whl

docs.title: Copy to specific architecture
docs.text: $ bash cp_wheels.sh --remove --arch x86-64-v3 --wheel <name>

docs.title: Force overwrite existing wheel in the wheelhouse
docs.text: $ bash cp_wheels.sh --force --wheel numpy-2.2.0+computecanada-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl

docs.title: Copy multiple matched wheels with GNU Parallel
docs.text: $ parallel bash cp_wheels.sh --remove --wheel ::: alphafold3-3.0.1+computecanada-cp31* numpy-*.whl

docs.title: manipulate_wheels.py
docs.text: This script allows direct manipulation of wheel archives, primarily to inspect or update metadata and package requirements without rebuilding from source.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py -h
usage: manipulate_wheels [-h] -w WHEELS [WHEELS ...] [-i] [-u UPDATE_REQ [UPDATE_REQ ...]]
                         [-a ADD_REQ [ADD_REQ ...]] [-r REMOVE_REQ [REMOVE_REQ ...]]
                         [--set_min_numpy SET_MIN_NUMPY] [--set_lt_numpy SET_LT_NUMPY]
                         [--inplace] [--force] [-p] [-v] [-t TAG]

Manipulate wheel files

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -w WHEELS [WHEELS ...], --wheels WHEELS [WHEELS ...]
                        Specifies which wheels to patch (default: None)
  -i, --insert_local_version
                        Adds the +computecanada local version (default: False)
  -u UPDATE_REQ [UPDATE_REQ ...], --update_req UPDATE_REQ [UPDATE_REQ ...]
                        Updates requirements of the wheel. (default: None)
  -a ADD_REQ [ADD_REQ ...], --add_req ADD_REQ [ADD_REQ ...]
                        Add requirements to the wheel. (default: None)
  -r REMOVE_REQ [REMOVE_REQ ...], --remove_req REMOVE_REQ [REMOVE_REQ ...]
                        Remove requirements from the wheel. (default: None)
  --set_min_numpy SET_MIN_NUMPY
                        Sets the minimum required numpy version. (default: None)
  --set_lt_numpy SET_LT_NUMPY
                        Sets the lower than (<) required numpy version. (default: None)
  --inplace             Work in the same directory as the existing wheel instead of a temporary location (default: False)
  --force               If combined with --inplace, overwrites existing wheel if the resulting wheel has the same name (default: False)
  -p, --print_req       Prints the current requirements (default: False)
  -v, --verbose         Displays information about what it is doing (default: False)
  -t TAG, --add_tag TAG
                        Specifies a tag to add to wheels (default: None)

docs.title: In-place Modification and --force
docs.text:
• By default, output wheels are generated into ./tmp.
  • Passing --inplace writes the output wheel to the directory of the source wheel.
  • If the new wheel has the exact same name as the existing wheel, manipulate_wheels.py will abort with an error unless --force is provided.

docs.title: Tag Placement (--add_tag)
docs.text: When adding a custom tag (such as --add_tag torch24): - If the wheel does not yet have a local version, +<tag> is appended. - If the wheel already contains a local version (e.g. +computecanada), the new tag is inserted immediately following the + sign (resulting in +torch24.computecanada).

docs.title: Requirement Narrowing for NumPy
docs.text: When --set_min_numpy or --set_lt_numpy is supplied, manipulate_wheels.py parses existing version constraints and automatically narrows overlapping bounds: - Combining existing >=1.19 with --set_min_numpy 1.22 resolves to >=1.22. - Conflicting or impossible version bounds will throw an error and abort.

docs.title: Print requirements
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py -p -w biopython-*.whl 
Resulting wheels will be in directory ./tmp
Requirements for wheel biopython-1.84+computecanada-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl:
==========================
numpy
==========================

docs.title: Add requirement
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py --inplace --force --add_req 'numpy' -w wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl 
Since --force was used, overwriting existing wheel
New wheel created wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl

$ ./manipulate_wheels.py -p -w wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl 
Resulting wheels will be in directory ./tmp
Requirements for wheel wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl:
==========================
pytest >= 6.0.0 ; extra == "test"
setuptools >= 65 ; extra == "test"
numpy
==========================

docs.title: Remove requirement
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py --inplace --force --remove_req 'numpy' -w wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl 
wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl: requirement numpy found. Removing it
Since --force was used, overwriting existing wheel
New wheel created wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: Update requirement
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py --inplace --force --update_req 'setuptools' -w wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl 
Since --force was used, overwriting existing wheel
New wheel created wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: Rename a requirement
docs.text:
Rename a requirement using the -> separator: 

$ ./manipulate_wheels.py -v -w wheel-0.2.2-py3-none-any.whl -u "faiss-cpu->faiss" "tensorflow (>=2.2.2)"
wheel-0.2.2-py3-none-any.whl: updating requirement faiss-cpu to faiss
wheel-0.2.2-py3-none-any.whl: updating requirement tensorflow (>=2.2.0) to tensorflow (>=2.2.2)
New wheel created tmp/wheel-0.2.2-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: Insert local tag (+computecanada)
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py --inplace -i -w wheel-0.2.2-py3-none-any.whl 
New wheel created wheel-0.2.2+computecanada-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: Insert custom tag
docs.text:
$ ./manipulate_wheels.py --inplace --add_tag custom -w wheel-0.45.1-py3-none-any.whl 
New wheel created wheel-0.45.1+custom-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: parbuild_wheel.sh
docs.text: Builds multiple versions and/or multiple Python wheels in parallel using GNU parallel. The script utilizes available CPU cores to execute separate build_wheel.sh instances concurrently.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Usage: parbuild_wheel.sh 
  --package <comma-separated list of package names>
  [--version <comma-separated list of versions>]
  [--python <comma-separated list of python versions>]
  [--requirements <requirements file>]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --package <names> Comma-separated list of packages to build (required unless --requirements is specified). --version <versions> Comma-separated list of package versions. If omitted, builds the latest version. --python <versions> Comma-separated list of Python versions. Defaults to all active Python versions in the current StdEnv. --requirements <file> Path to a requirements file specifying packages and optional versions to build.

docs.title: Standard Environment & Behavior
docs.text:
• StdEnv 2026 (2026): Excludes Python versions $\le$ 3.13, targeting Python 3.14+.
  • StdEnv 2023 (2023): Excludes Python versions $\le$ 3.10, targeting Python 3.11 to 3.14.
  • Non-recursive Builds: Underlying invocations call build_wheel.sh with --recursive 0 and --verbose 3 so that concurrent jobs do not build duplicate dependencies.

docs.title: Requirements File Syntax
docs.text: When passing --requirements <file>, parbuild_wheel.sh processes: - Pinned packages (package==version): Builds the specified version across all selected Python versions. - Unpinned packages (package): Builds the latest PyPI version across all selected Python versions. - Trailing semicolons (often found in freeze files) are automatically stripped. Other complex constraint specifiers (such as >=, <, or environment markers) should be adapted to == or unpinned lines.

docs.title: Output Logs & Process Control
docs.text:
• Individual Build Logs: Written to build-{package}-{version}-py{python}.log (or build-{package}-py{python}.log for unpinned builds) in the current directory.
  • Commands List: Commands to be run are generated into <PID>.cmds.
  • Parallel Job Log: Execution status for all jobs is recorded in <PID>.log and summarized upon completion.
  • Cancelling Jobs: Press Ctrl+C in the terminal, or terminate running parallel tasks with: 
    $ killall -TERM parallel

docs.title: Build package across all default Python versions
docs.text: $ bash parbuild_wheel.sh --package biopython

docs.title: Build multiple packages in parallel
docs.text: $ bash parbuild_wheel.sh --package numpy,scipy,pandas

docs.title: Build multiple versions of a package
docs.text: $ bash parbuild_wheel.sh --package biopython --version 1.83,1.84

docs.title: Build specific Python versions
docs.text: $ bash parbuild_wheel.sh --package biopython --python 3.11,3.12

docs.title: Batch build from a requirements file
docs.text: $ bash parbuild_wheel.sh --requirements requirements.txt

docs.title: unmanylinuxize.sh
docs.text:
Downloads a pre-built manylinux wheel from PyPI, an external wheel index, or a direct URL, and patches its RPATH and metadata to make it compatible with the DRAC software stack.

Build from source when possible

Prefer building from source using build_wheel.sh when possible to benefit from optimization and consistent library linkage.

Packages distributed as binary wheels often carry manylinux tags in their filenames. Out of the box, these wheels are typically incompatible with our software stack because libraries reside in custom CVMFS paths rather than standard system directories.

unmanylinuxize.sh downloads the wheel, patches RPATHs using setrpaths, applies optional package-specific patch commands, renames the manylinux platform tag to linux_x86_64, and appends the +computecanada local version tag.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Usage: unmanylinuxize.sh 
  --package <package name> 
  [--version <version>]
  [--python <comma separated list of python versions>]
  [--add_path <rpath>]
  [--add_origin]
  [--find_links https://index.url | --url https://direct.url.to.wheel.whl]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --package <name> Python package name (required unless --url is specified). --version <version> Package version to download (defaults to latest if omitted). --python <versions> Comma-separated list of Python versions to download for. Defaults to all active Python versions in the current StdEnv. --add_path <rpath> Additional directory path(s) to append to the RPATH using setrpaths --add_path <rpath> --any_interpreter. --add_origin Flag to add $ORIGIN to the RPATH via setrpaths --add_origin. --find_links <url> Custom index URL to search for wheels (sets PIP_FIND_LINKS). --url <url> Direct URL to download a specific .whl file using wget.

docs.title: Standard Environment & Behavior
docs.text:
• StdEnv 2026 (2026): Excludes Python versions <=3.13, downloading for Python 3.14+.
  • StdEnv 2023 (2023): Excludes Python versions <=3.10, downloading for Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.
  • Pure Python & ABI3 Early Exit: If a downloaded wheel is py3-none-any, py2.py3-none-any, or ABI3 compatible (cp*-abi3), downloading terminates after the first Python version since the artifact is compatible across all versions.
  • Configuration Recipes: Sources configuration recipes from config/ (config/<package>-<version>.sh or config/<package>.sh), executing any defined PATCH_WHEEL_COMMANDS.

docs.title: Download and patch specific version
docs.text: $ bash unmanylinuxize.sh --package sktime --version 0.21.1

docs.title: Specific Python version
docs.text: $ bash unmanylinuxize.sh --package sktime --version 0.21.1 --python 3.11

docs.title: Add specific library RPATH
docs.text:
Preload required modules and add library directories to RPATH: 

$ module load cuda/12 cudnn/9
$ bash unmanylinuxize.sh --package open3d --add_path $EBROOTCUDACORE/lib/:$EBROOTCUDNN/lib

docs.title: Add $ORIGIN to RPATH
docs.text:
Useful for wheels that bundle shared libraries in internal directories and locate them relative to $ORIGIN: 

$ bash unmanylinuxize.sh --package mypkg --version 1.0.0 --add_origin

docs.title: Download from alternative index
docs.text: $ bash unmanylinuxize.sh --package cupy-cuda12x --find_links https://pypi.nvidia.com

docs.title: Download from direct URL
docs.text: $ bash unmanylinuxize.sh --url https://github.com/example/pkg/releases/download/v1.0.0/pkg-1.0.0-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl

docs.title: wheel_architecture.sh
docs.text: Analyzes the contents of a wheel and predicts the appropriate compatibility layer and sub-directory of the wheelhouse where the wheel should be placed.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Usage: wheel_architecture.sh <FILENAME>.whl

docs.title: Compatibility Layers and Architectures
docs.text: Layer Architecture Description generic generic Generic across Nix and Gentoo environments, without architecture-specific CPU extensions. nix generic Requires the Nix compatibility layer; not architecture-dependent. gentoo generic Requires Gentoo prefix; not architecture-dependent. gentoo2020 generic Compatible with Gentoo 2020 environment. gentoo2020 sse3 / avx / avx2 / avx512 Requires Gentoo 2020 and depends on libraries in the respective architecture path. gentoo2023 generic Requires Gentoo 2023; not architecture-dependent. gentoo2023 x86-64-v3 Requires Gentoo 2023 and depends on libraries in x86-64-v3. gentoo2023 x86-64-v4 Requires Gentoo 2023 and depends on libraries in x86-64-v4. gentoo2026 generic Requires Gentoo 2026; not architecture-dependent. gentoo2026 x86-64-v3 Requires Gentoo 2026 and depends on libraries in x86-64-v3. gentoo2026 x86-64-v4 Requires Gentoo 2026 and depends on libraries in x86-64-v4. unknown generic Cannot satisfy glibc or library dependencies in standard layers, or contains local paths.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Extraction & Binary Inspection: Unpacks the wheel into a temporary directory and inspects all ELF binaries and shared objects (.so).
  2. Local RPATH Safety Check: Verifies that no binaries contain RPATH entries referencing user directories (/home/ or /.local/). Wheels containing local RPATHs are rejected across all layers and classified as unknown to prevent non-portable or user-tainted builds from entering the central wheelhouse.
  3. glibc Requirement Verification: Extracts required GLIBC_ versions from binaries and compares them against the glibc version provided by Nix, Gentoo 2020, Gentoo 2023, and Gentoo 2026.
  4. Library Dependency Resolution: Runs the corresponding ldd for each layer to detect missing shared libraries (ignoring self-contained libraries bundled inside the wheel).
  5. Architecture Detection: Analyzes RPATH entries for CPU architecture directories (sse3, avx, avx2, avx512, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4). Standard core paths (such as /x86-64-v3/Core/) are excluded so pure Python or standard runtime wheels remain generic.

Note

While the script makes automated predictions, certain packages may depend on runtime libraries only present in virtual environments or specific modules. Always verify the output before deployment.

docs.title: Pure Python wheel
docs.text:
$ bash wheel_architecture.sh transformers-4.49.0+computecanada-py3-none-any.whl
generic generic
The wheel contains no compiled extensions or shared objects.

docs.title: Architecture-specific wheel
docs.text:
$ bash wheel_architecture.sh pyFFTW-0.13.1+computecanada-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl
...
gentoo2023 x86-64-v3
This wheel depends on FFTW libraries located in the x86-64-v3 architecture path.

docs.title: Wheel with local RPATH warning
docs.text:
$ bash wheel_architecture.sh custom_pkg-1.0.0+computecanada-cp311-cp311-linux_x86_64.whl
./custom_pkg/_ext.so contains a local rpath, rpath=/home/user/.local/lib:...
unknown generic
The wheel contains local user paths and must be rebuilt cleanly before deployment.

docs.title: Missing shared objects
docs.text:
Some packages link against external libraries that will be installed into a virtual environment at runtime (e.g. PyTorch): 

$ bash wheel_architecture.sh torchtext-0.18.0+computecanada-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl
./torchtext/_torchtext.so requires a glibc more recent than that provided by Gentoo 2020: 2.34 > 2.30
    libtorch_python.so => not found
    libc10.so => not found
    libtorch.so => not found
unknown generic
Since libtorch.so is missing during inspection, wheel_architecture.sh reports unknown. If you know the package targets Gentoo 2023/2026, deploy it explicitly with cp_wheels.sh --arch generic.
